verdict.rationale: Metorial's SDK documents OAuth flows that let your users authorize their own accounts. The platform docs say each user connects their own apps and keeps their own permissions rather than sharing broad credentials, so per-user connected accounts are a first-party capability. However, the evidence never documents issuing per-end-user scoped tokens or how a session is bound to one specific user's credentials; session tool filters are a separate control. Missing for 10: documented per-end-user scoped token issuance, explicit binding of sessions or agents to an individual user's OAuth credentials, hands-on corroboration of credential isolation between users.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials

citations.quote: OAuth lets your users authorize access to their accounts on services like Slack, GitHub, Google Calendar, and more.
Instead of sharing broad credentials or over-scoped service accounts, each user connects their own apps and keeps the permissions they should have.
Workforce is where admins turn user-authorized tool access into something AI agents and applications can use.
